_comment: Defaults for the 'Additional Description' tab (66 attributes).
Every key here is a REAL field name captured by `npm run scan balloon-decoration`.
These are the answers that are the same for most WishWorks balloon/party listings —
a product file only needs to state what differs.
Multi-value fields take arrays. Fields that don't apply to a given product are simply
left out (the hand-fan / blowout / cracker / battery attributes below are part of this
category but irrelevant to balloon kits, so they're deliberately absent).
DELIBERATELY BLANK (24 fields): Handle*, Hand Fan Type, Animal Type, Guardstick/Rib/Leaf
Material, Leaf Shape, Printed Text, Mouthpiece/Tube*, Burn Time, Visual Effects, Sound
Features, Cracker Type, Powered by, Power Requirement, Type/Number of Batteries, Other*.
This category is shared with hand fans, blowouts, crackers and battery toys — inventing
values there is how listings fail QC. Blank is the correct answer, not a gap.
NO COMMAS inside any array value: Flipkart splits multi-value fields on ','.
_dimensions: The Dimensions block, in INCHES, added 2026-08-12 from Vansh's screenshot of the tab he had
just filled by hand. Universal because he asked for it to be: 'lets make it universal for
every listing that we do'. These describe the PACKED parcel — flat, uninflated, foil folded.
SAFE TO PUT HERE ONLY SINCE THE DEFAULTS BECAME PER-TAB (loadProduct's DefaultsTab).
'Height' also exists in Package Details on the Price/Stock tab, where it is CENTIMETRES, and
before the split this file's 1.5 would have been typed into both — inches here, cm there.
That is WW-123 exactly. Do not move these into a shared file.
WEIGHT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT and must stay absent. It is the one number here a courier
re-measures and bills back (WW-055), it differs per kit, and it carries a UNIT PICKER that has
to agree with it — packaging.ts writes 'Weight' and 'Weight (unit)' together from the measured
parcel, which is the only place that pairing is guaranteed correct. A universal weight would
be typed into every listing whose parcel was never weighed, which is the failure WW-055 is.
DIAMETER IS ALSO ABSENT, and that is an answer to a question, not an oversight. Vansh asked
2026-08-12: 'is diameter of our use, and will it be diameter of balloon after blowing air in
it?' This block describes the PACKED PARCEL — a flat 7 x 8 x 1.5 in bag has no diameter, and
putting an INFLATED balloon's diameter in it mixes the two states C-052 was logged for. The
field is optional on the form. Fill it only for a product that is genuinely round, with a
figure from the INVENTORY, which is what PROMPT-product.md already says.
_handle: HANDLE IS A REAL ANSWER, NOT FILLER. It sat in PROMPT-product.md's leave-out list with the
hand-fan attributes, but 'does this product have a handle' has a true answer for a balloon
kit and the answer is No — same family as Foldable and Carry Bag Included, which have been
here from the start. Handle Shape and Handle Material stay out: they are hand-fan fields and
only mean anything once Handle is Yes.
It is a dropdown, and the scan did not record its options. If Flipkart does not offer 'No'
the fill reports what it DOES offer and types nothing — visible, never silently wrong.
_occasion: OCCASION IS NOT HERE ANY MORE, and it must not come back. It was Birthday + Anniversary +
Baby Shower, which is right for a birthday kit and FALSE for every other kind we sell — an
Annaprashan kit went out claiming Birthday because ChatGPT omitted the field and this filled
it. A wrong value is worse than a missing one, and the default made the wrong one invisible.
Vansh, 2026-08-12: 'we should let the prompt chatgpt decide it'. PROMPT-product.md now works
the occasion out from the banner wording, the props and the INVENTORY, and the form's field
is free text (kind: pills in the scan), so any real occasion is a valid answer. Missing now
means an empty box, which is visible.
Precautions: Keep away from fire and sharp objects
Not suitable for children under 3 years - choking hazard
Not Covered in Warranty: Damage due to misuse, over-inflation or normal wear
